record: measured probe: does a real ResearchOS CLI entry exist, and can the registry dispatch it?

cli_entry_runs_directly.source: apps/cli/main.go, package main, 86 lines, const productName = researchos

second_probe.reading: honest NOT_FOUND because no host is running. The entry is real and refuses rather than inventing a host, which is the behaviour the CLI is supposed to have before W02 host assembly.

dispatcher_answer_on_the_key.reading: zero assertions with NOT_IMPLEMENTED is the registry correctly refusing to pretend. It is not a PASS and must never be presented as one - the same rule that keeps an empty selector result out of receipts.

registry_state.path_ownership: CLI maps to apps/cli (W02-02); the entry exists because W02-02 and W02-03 are ACCEPTED, but nobody has bound the key that dispatches it

blast_radius_of_binding_this_key: the v2.4 registry supersedes v2.0 per key, so binding cli.entry_run changes resolution only for invocations of that key, and its selectors are wildcards, so no other key flips. commands.json is nevertheless hash-pinned by several ACCEPTED receipts, so the binding needs a before-baseline row for this key plus a computed erratum beside every accepted receipt that hashes the file. The pinned receipts themselves are never edited.
consequence_for_W01_G03: own_cli_entry_present asks for a filename containing researchos under apps/cli. The entry exists and runs, so the flag measures the wrong thing; and even with the flag fixed the gate would still fail because the key is UNBOUND. G03 needs both a bound dispatchable CLI key and a flag that asks the dispatcher rather than a directory listing.

prepared_not_applied.why_unapplied: it rewrites execution/v2.4/commands.json, which the W13-01 receipt under round-2 review hashes as an artifact; the guard detects an open review request and refuses --apply, which was verified by the registry hash being identical before and after the refused run
prepared_not_applied.next_step_once_a_review_lands: run the script with --apply, then re-resolve W01-G03 read-only, replace the filename flag with a dispatch test inside the card that owns qualification/v2.4, and re-measure the gate

corrections.false_claim_in_this_file_and_in_d88e0481: the prepared_not_applied note said the guard refusal was the branch exercised here. It was not. The first guard asked whether a card had ANY verdict file, and W13-01 already holds a round-1 verdict, so the script found zero reviews in flight and wrote a binding plan while a live round-2 review sat on the tree. The commit message repeated that as a fact.
corrections.what_was_done_about_it: the guard now keys on the open request: a card is under review when it has REVIEW_REQUEST_ROUND<N>.md without a matching independent_review_round<N>.json, or a REWORK status. Re-run: plan mode reports W13-01 in flight (receipt sha ffe33eca), and --apply refuses; execution/v2.4/commands.json hashes 8813771b258f2aee both before and after the refused apply, so no write happened.
corrections.limitation_of_this_reading: the exit code of the refused --apply run was masked by piping through tail, so the refusal is proved by the unchanged registry hash and the printed refusal line, not by an observed non-zero status in that shell
